title: Your Life as an Astronaut at Every Level (Most Never Fly)
hook: Boot touches dust that hasn't felt one in over fifty years. Black sky, no wind, but your chest tightens anyway. Houston's voice crackles, waiting on the first words history gets to keep. Don't say it yet.
body: POV: a composite civilian engineer who climbs the real, documented NASA astronaut ladder -- Applicant (VERIFIED: 8,000+ applied to the 2024 selection cycle, only 10 chosen) to Astronaut Candidate/ASCAN (2 years at Johnson Space Center: T-38 supersonic jets, the Neutral Buoyancy Lab, a fixed GS-12 salary) to Astronaut, unassigned (a real 5-10+ year wait for a flight; some selected astronauts never fly at all) to a first ISS flight (a Crew Dragon seat costs NASA roughly $55 million) to Veteran/EVA Specialist (the midpoint reversal is grounded in the real July 16, 2013 incident where ESA astronaut Luca Parmitano's helmet filled with over a liter of water mid-spacewalk, happening here to a FICTIONAL COMPOSITE protagonist) to Expedition Commander (the ISS program has cost its partner nations an estimated $150 billion) to Chief Astronaut Office (deciding who flies, grounding people for medical reasons) to an Artemis-era lunar commander -- grounded in NASA's real, repeatedly-delayed Artemis program; no human has stood on the Moon since Apollo 17 in December 1972. Voss, Sable Chen, Mara, Junie, and Petrova are a FICTIONAL COMPOSITE; no real astronaut is depicted as this episode's protagonist. Watch the whole series -- every life, every level, every ladder somebody has to climb from the bottom. For educational and entertainment purposes.
pinned: Real fact: NASA's 2024 astronaut selection cycle drew more than 8,000 applicants for 10 spots -- lower odds than any Ivy League school. And even getting picked doesn't guarantee a flight: some selected astronauts wait a decade for a mission, and some never fly at all. Which level do you think is the hardest to survive: the wait, or the spacewalk?
poll: Which level costs the most? LEVEL 03 (Astronaut, Unassigned -- years of waiting, no guarantee) / LEVEL 05 (Veteran/EVA Specialist -- 1.5 liters of water inside your helmet) / LEVEL 07 (Chief Astronaut Office -- grounding your own mentor) / LEVEL 08 (Artemis Commander -- $93B moves around you, your paycheck doesn't move at all)
